title: Sharp Separable-Effect Bounds for Competing Risks under Scheduled Inspections

proof_attempt_summary: The derivation established supporting compatibility, interval-attainment, recursion, ceiling-sensitivity, mesh-width, and confidence-inversion results. It did not prove the headline universal finite-switch bound B or equality with a finite evaluable program; those were left open, so the required kernel was not delivered and the boundary consult found no distinct faithful retry.
tldr: Scheduled inspections identify factual competing-event bin probabilities but erase the within-bin ordering needed to splice the cause-1 hazard from arm 1 with the cause-2 hazard from arm 0. Conditional on an externally calibrated ceiling \(L\) imposed uniformly across the four cause-by-arm hazards, disclosed as a novel maintained sensitivity restriction, the sharp component-risk interval is characterized by one-bin incidence-survival support envelopes and an exact backward recursion; replacing \(L\) by a conservative \(\bar L\ge L\) can only enlarge the interval. Whether every envelope extremum admits a parameter-uniform bound on the number of shared constant-control subintervals remains open; the note specifies a positive-cell two-cycle constrained-Hessian kill test for that question. The matched mesh-width theorem and finite-sample multinomial inversion do not claim such a finite representation.
gap: Resolved-time separable-effect theory identifies the cross-arm hazard integral, and discrete competing-risk partial-identification theory treats latent-duration distributions, but neither characterizes the sharp grouped-data component-risk frontier conditional on a transparently calibrated intensity ceiling or its monotone sensitivity expansion when that ceiling is relaxed.
fill: The project treats \(L\) as an externally calibrated maintained restriction, derives nested identified sets under \(L\) and \(\bar L\), builds the attainable survival-flow frontier, and seeks an explicit universal common-piece bound through the specified cycle-compression predicate. It then composes local envelopes into globally sharp endpoints, derives the matched inspection-mesh modulus, and projects a simultaneous multinomial confidence region through the certified endpoint map.
